subject: High latency & intermittent 504s from Stratus Fidelity - needing exec visibility
messages:
From: Oliver Cho <oliver.cho@stratusfidelity.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: High latency & 504s: inference.redwood endpoints (prod)

Hi Avery,

We're seeing sustained latency spikes and intermittent 504s from our production jobs hitting inference.redwood in us-west-2 starting ~08:45 PDT this morning.  P95 token latency is ~2.4s (normally ~300-400ms) and about 1.5% of requests return 504s.  This is impacting our real-time scoring pipeline.  We've run retries but it compounds latency.

I've attached a short pcap from a couple of failed calls and a route snapshot. Can you confirm whether there are any known peering changes or maintenance on your side? We need an ETA for a fix or a mitigation approach.

Attachments: pcap_trace-20280308.zip, route-ops-snapshot.txt

Thanks,
Oliver
Sr. SRE, Stratus Fidelity
oliver.cho@stratusfidelity.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-08T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency & 504s — preliminary findings

Short update / preliminary findings from infra triage (SRE):

Root-cause hypothesis (interim):
1) Asymmetric peering after a route propagation hiccup caused a subset of Stratus traffic to egress via a different transit provider, adding ~200-700ms extra RTT for the affected paths.
2) Their DNS TTL for the inference endpoint is low (30s) and combined with our downstream proxy health probes caused frequent connection churn. The churn invalidated firewall session state on our edge proxies because session affinity & NAT tables didn't persist across the transient path change. This resulted in TCP retransmits and a small percent of connections timing out (504).
3) The impact surface was amplified for inference-02 because that cluster's fronting proxies were on the peering path that hit the transit provider with higher latency.

Evidence: pcap shows many duplicate SYNs and late SYN-ACKs; route snapshot shows divergent next-hops correlating with spikes.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (13:20 PDT):
- Re-routed Stratus customer tag traffic away from inference-02 to inference-01 (drain-inflight, graceful).
- Bumped proxy session timeout to retain NAT mappings an additional 60s for affected frontends.
- Opened Jira INF-7123 to track permanent peering update & control-plane guardrails.

Short-term ask for customer: can they temporarily raise internal DNS TTL to 120s while we stabilize? That will reduce churn and give the peering fix time to propagate.

Next steps:
- Marcus to coordinate with Network Ops on peering route correction and confirm routes converge consistently (ETA 24 hours).
- SRE to monitor p95 and 504s; if still above thresholds we'll fail traffic to a warm standby region (us-west-1) as an emergency fallback.

I'll keep everyone posted.

-Stephanie
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Cho <oliver.cho@stratusfidelity.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-08T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 504s: inference.redwood endpoints (prod) — short-term actions taken

Oliver — quick update and ask:

What we did (13:20 PDT):
- Shifted Stratus traffic away from inference-02 to inference-01 to avoid the affected peering path.
- Increased proxy NAT/session retention to reduce session churn.
- Opened ticket INF-7123 for the peering route convergence and longer-term fix.

What we need from you:
- If possible, temporarily increase your DNS TTL for inference endpoint to 120s for the next 24 hours. This will significantly reduce client-side churn while we stabilize.
- Send any additional X-Request-IDs for observed 504s if you find them.

Observed impact so far: p95 latency down to ~600–750ms, 504s dropped to ~0.2% in the 30 minutes after the shift. We're continuing to watch metrics and traces.

I'll be on standby for a call if you'd like (15m).

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
avery_johnson@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Cho <oliver.cho@stratusfidelity.com>, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 504s: inference.redwood endpoints (prod) — update & permanent plan

Oliver / Avery — final update from Network Ops: the peering provider experienced a transient route flap during their upstream config push on 2028-03-08 08:55 PDT which caused a subset of prefixes to prefer an alternate transit path. We coordinated with them and validated route convergence this afternoon.

Permanent remediation plan (INF-7123):
- Apply stricter BGP prepending and community tags to ensure deterministic egress for customer-facing frontends (ETA 48 hours).
- Add control-plane validations to detect asymmetric next-hops and auto-flag traffic to alternate clusters before user impact (ETA 2 weeks).
- Lower our front-end proxy sensitivity to session table rebalances by making NAT mappings sticky per-client-subnet when feasible (ETA 1 week).

We've documented the timeline and attached the packet summary to the Jira. Please let us know if you'd like a post-mortem + exec-briefing for your leadership.

Marcus Lin
Network Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
